item.research_question: What are the deformation mechanisms and strain-hardening behaviors of 〈001〉-oriented fcc dual-phase FeCoCrNiAl0.5 at room and cryogenic temperatures?
item.material_system: FeCoCrNiAl0.5 (dual-phase fcc dendrites with bcc/B2 interdendritic network and precipitates)
item.processing_route: Bridgman technique ingot preparation in Ar atmosphere, homogenization at 1373K for 24 h, annealing at 1123K for 1 h, water quench, electro-discharge machining (EDM) to 4 mm × 4 mm × 8 mm, grinding to 4000 grit, vibration-polishing for EBSD
item.test_conditions: Uniaxial compression at 77K (liquid nitrogen) and 293K (room temperature) up to ~35% total axial strain; ex-situ digital image correlation (DIC) with 0.08 μm/pixel resolution; EBSD and TEM analysis
key_findings: Hardening rate saturates at ~6 GPa above 23% total axial strain at both 77K and 293K.
Stress levels exceed 1800 MPa at ~35% total axial strain without failure at either temperature.
The fcc component carries the larger part of the plastic strain (mean strain ~3% in fcc vs ~1% in bcc/B2 at ~2% total strain).
Deformation twinning is observed in the fcc phase at both 77K and 293K, but only above 23% axial strain.
Slip activity is found exclusively in the bcc/B2 phase, with no deformation twinning observed there.
Increasing temperature from 77K to 293K raises stress levels by 250–350 MPa but leaves the hardening rate variation unaffected.
The hardening rate increase of >2 GPa beyond 23% strain is present even at room temperature.
item.mechanism: The authors attribute the substantial hardening to the combined action of fcc–bcc/B2 interphase boundaries acting as obstacles, extensive deformation twinning in the fcc phase which strongly hardens secondary systems, and fine dense bcc/B2 precipitates inside the fcc dendrites. They specifically note that twin-related interactions are far more important for strengthening than pure slip interactions, and that dislocation reactions at fcc-bcc/B2 interfaces and fcc twin boundaries create residual barriers.
item.limitations: The text does not explicitly state limitations of the study, though it notes that the intricate microstructure and chemical gradients add intricacy to the stress-strain response and that further work is needed to unravel the influence of the minor phase volume fraction and distribution.
item.future_work: The authors propose that future work should focus on in-situ DIC, nanomechanical testing, and varying heterointerface amounts to differentiate contributions. They also suggest work on the effects of composition on intrinsic energy barriers and composition optimization to develop novel HEAs with higher work-hardening.
quotes: As a result, the hardening rate associated saturates at the unusual high value of ~6 GPa.
These results may guide future advancements in the design of novel alloys with superior toughening characteristics.
We surmise that the reason for the high degree of strain hardening beyond 23% axial strain is deformation-induced twinning.
